## Design note

Point-and-squirt in any weather. Instant dual-clutch shifts and AWD launches make it brutally quick to 100 km/h for its power, and it is the most forgiving fast car in the roster. The price is a front-heavy chassis that understeers when pushed and a ceiling the rear-drive cars break through on open roads.

## How this car breaks

Modern UHSS cell and long crumple rails make it one of the safest cabins on the list; frontals crush the nose but rarely the occupants. The rear coupling and prop shaft run under the floor, so heavy kerb or sill strikes can kill drive to the rear. Plastic everywhere outside the cell: cheap to bend, cheap to fix.

## Inertia

Box approximation about the CG, scaled for mass concentration (`k < 1`: mass near the centre, e.g. mid-engine; `k → 1`: mass at the ends):

```
I_roll  = k_r · m·(W² + H²)/12
I_pitch = k_p · m·(L² + H²)/12
I_yaw   = k_y · m·(W² + L²)/12
```

| Axis | Box (kg·m²) | k | `inertia_kgm2` |
|---|---|---|---|
| roll | 688 | 0.80 | 550 |
| pitch | 2642 | 0.90 | 2380 |
| yaw | 2793 | 0.92 | 2570 |

## Drivetrain

6-speed dual-clutch, on-demand clutch-pack rear coupling (95 % front until the fronts slip 5 %, then up to 50 % rear), open diffs with brake-based torque vectoring (assist). Layout **on-demand AWD, 95 % front with the coupling open, up to 50 % rear once the fronts out-spin the rears by 5 %**; front diff: open; rear diff: open. Clutch capacity 1.40 × peak torque = 530 N·m. Shift time 0.18 s.

| Gear | Ratio | Overall | km/h @ redline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3.46 | 12.63 | 60 |
| 2 | 2.15 | 7.85 | 97 |
| 3 | 1.45 | 5.29 | 143 |
| 4 | 1.10 | 4.02 | 189 |
| 5 | 0.87 | 3.18 | 238 |
| 6 | 0.71 | 2.59 | 292 |

Final drive 3.65, reverse 3.00. Speeds use the driven-wheel loaded radius 0.309 m.

## Suspension

Springs from ride frequency, `k = m_s·(2πf)²` with sprung corner mass `m_s = axle load/2 − unsprung`; dampers `c = 2ζ·√(k·m_s)`, ζ = 0.30 bump, rebound = 1.5 × bump.

| Axle | m_s | f | Wheel rate k | Bump c | Rebound c | Travel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Front | 444 kg | 1.80 Hz | 56800 N/m | 3020 N·s/m | 4530 N·s/m | 0.15 m |
| Rear | 289 kg | 1.90 Hz | 41200 N/m | 2070 N·s/m | 3100 N·s/m | 0.16 m |

Round 12b ride rule (A): the file carries the derived dampers × 1.2 bump / × 1.6 rebound (rebound ≈ 2 × bump), after any tunes below: **3620 / 7250 N·s/m F, 2480 / 4960 N·s/m R** (bump / rebound).

Anti-roll bars from a roll-gradient target of 2.2°/g with 55% of roll stiffness at the front. Roll arm h − h_rc = 0.424 m (roll centres 0.08 m F / 0.12 m R). Required total K_φ = m·g·arm/φ = 168395 N·m/rad; springs give k·t²/2 = 66961 F / 46940 R N·m/rad; bars supply the rest as `arb_n_per_m = K_bar/t²` = **10900 F / 12600 R N/m** (clamped at ≥ 0). Resulting gradient 2.2°/g, front share 55%. Bump stops 170000 N/m.

Alignment: camber -0.8° F / -1.3° R, toe +0.00° F / +0.20° R (+ = in), caster 7.0°.

## Brakes

Full-pedal line pressure 100 bar.

- Front: 340 mm disc, pistons per side 60 mm → A = 28.3 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 145 mm, pad μ = 0.42: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.42·100 bar·28.3 cm²·0.145 m = **3444 N·m**
- Rear: 310 mm disc, pistons per side 41 mm → A = 13.2 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 130 mm, pad μ = 0.4: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.4·100 bar·13.2 cm²·0.130 m = **1373 N·m**

ABS ceiling: caliper capacity 3444 / 1373 N·m exceeds 1.5 × the front lock torque on this car's tire (peak μ 1.20), which `wp_vehicle`'s ABS cannot modulate (it releases to a fraction of the commanded torque, so an oversized caliper keeps the wheel locked). Both axles scaled by 0.98 → **3380 / 1350 N·m**. Remove when 02's ABS modulates relative to lock torque.

Lock check at 1 g on μ = 1 (load transfer m·a·h/L): front needs 1880 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.80×), rear needs 477 N·m/wheel (capacity 2.83×).

`wp_vehicle` gives the axle `bias_front` favours its full `max_torque_*` and scales the other by (1 − b)/b, so `max_torque_*` holds the caliper capacity per wheel and `bias_front` acts as the proportioning valve: the rear is trimmed to the same lock margin as the front (ideal rear = T_f · lock_r/lock_f = 857 N·m), never boosted above its caliper capacity. Rear capacity exceeds that, so `bias_front` = T_r/(T_r + ideal) = **0.612** → delivered 3380 N·m front / 856 N·m rear per wheel at full pedal. Handbrake 1410 N·m per rear wheel.

## Steering

Ratio 13.6:1. Kerb-to-kerb turning circle 10.9 m → outer-front path radius 5.34 m, rear-axle-centre radius 3.88 m → mean road-wheel lock δ = atan(L/R) = **0.596 rad (34.2°)** (outer 29.5°, inner 40.2° at full Ackermann; `ackermann_frac` 0.60). Rack speed 1.7 rad/s.

## Damage lattice (`data/lattices/lindwurm_4t.json`)

271 nodes, 1778 beams, 8 detachables, 21 component mounts.

- Generated with `gen-lattice --id lindwurm_4t --profile hatch --width 1.8 --length 4.28 --height 1.44 --wheelbase 2.63 --mass 342.0 --car-mass 1554.5 --clearance 0.13 --front-overhang 0.9 --strength 1.0` (22% of vehicle mass in the lattice; strength from durability class 3).
- Era `2010s`: gen-lattice's default HSS passenger cell kept as is.
- Steel hood: 105 hood beams aluminum → mild_steel.
- Detachables: steel bumpers ×2.3 break impulse / ×4 mass; steel hood ×1.4 / ×1.6.
- Luggage bay: 13 Cabin nodes behind the rear seatback (y < -1.21 m, rear axle +0.10 m) relabelled FrameRear — the passenger cell ends at the seatback, as on a real two-box body.
- Transverse engine: gearbox mounted on the left end of the engine block (gen-lattice places it in the tunnel at the firewall, as for FR).
